content.title: About
content.content: Sponge cake is a light, airy pastry typically made from eggs, sugar, flour, and a small amount of fat. It serves as a base for many desserts, can be soaked with syrup, and topped with cream, fruit, or glaze.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sponge cake originated in Europe in the 19th century as a lighter alternative to heavy pies.
Traditional French génoise relies solely on the volume of beaten eggs, without any leavening agents.
In Japan, "sporki" – sponge roll cakes covered with sweet glaze – are a popular treat.
Sponge layers are often used in layered cakes, each layer being brushed with different syrups.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Sponge cake provides carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Classic recipes contain little butter, making it less calorie‑dense than many other cakes.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The porous structure aids digestion, especially for those with mild gastrointestinal issues.

items.title: Egg or gluten allergy
items.content: Sponge cake contains eggs and wheat flour, which can trigger reactions in allergic individuals.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: The high sugar and simple carbohydrate content may cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sponge cake can be enjoyed on its own, sliced and served with berry sauce, used as a base for layered cakes, roulades, panna cotta, or simply toasted and dusted with powdered sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sponge cake in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freeze it, wrapped tightly in plastic film.
